idea: Why water pipes make unusual noises
title: Decoding Strange Pipe Noises in Your Home
description: If your pipes bang, whistle, or creak when you run water, your plumbing system is sending you a message. High-pitched whistling often indicates excessive water pressure or a worn valve washer restricting flow. Loud banging—known as water hammer—occurs when fast-flowing water stops abruptly, sending a physical shockwave through the line. Creaking sounds usually happen when hot water pipes expand and rub against wooden framing. Installing water hammer arrestors, tightening loose pipe straps, or adjusting a pressure reducing valve can quiet your system and prevent stress on joints. Have a licensed plumber evaluate persistent noises before vibrations cause hidden leaks.
